Find your LinkedIn QR code in the app

LinkedIn gives every member a personal QR code in the mobile app, for personal profiles only. Menu labels can change slightly with app updates.

  1. Open the LinkedIn app and tap the search bar at the top.
  2. Tap the QR code icon at the right end of the search bar.
  3. Open the My code tab to see your code.
  4. Use Share my code or Save to photos (Android has a save-to-gallery option).

Why make a custom code for your resume?

A screenshot of the in-app code looks fine on a phone but loses quality in a printed resume or a placement brochure. A custom code gives you a clean PNG or vector SVG that stays sharp at any size, in colors that suit your resume design.

It also works for company pages, so startups and small businesses can print a code that leads to their LinkedIn page, something the personal in-app code cannot do.

How to create a LinkedIn QR code

It takes a minute.

  1. Copy your LinkedIn address. It looks like linkedin.com/in/your-name for people or linkedin.com/company/your-company for companies.
  2. Paste it into the field above.
  3. Pick a dark color on a light background for the best scan reliability.
  4. Download the PNG for a Word or PDF resume, or the SVG for print.
  5. Scan it with your phone before you send or print your resume.

Consider customising your LinkedIn URL first in your profile settings. A cleaner link makes a simpler code, and changing the URL later breaks any codes you already printed.

Tips before you use it

Make sure the profile behind the code is worth scanning.

  • Update your headline, photo and About section before adding the code to your resume.
  • Keep the code at least about 1 inch (2.5 cm) wide on paper, with blank space around it.
  • Check your privacy settings. Make sure your public profile is visible to people who are not signed in, if you want recruiters to see it.
  • Test on iPhone and Android before you send the final PDF.
